title: Kubernetes in 60 seconds
caption: Kubernetes in 60 seconds: you describe what should be running, and it keeps making that true. #kubernetes #devops #cloud

scenes.title: Kubernetes
scenes.say: A hundred containers. One just crashed. Who restarts it?
One container is easy. A hundred containers across twenty servers, while one of them just died, is not.

scenes.code:
kind: Deployment
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - image: my-app:1.4
scenes.say: With Kubernetes you don't say what to do. You describe what should exist: three copies of this image.
Then it works constantly to make that true.

items.title: Heals
items.text: a container dies, it starts another
items.say: A container dies, it starts a new one.

items.title: Scales
items.say: Traffic grows, it can add copies.

items.title: Rolls out
items.text: new version, one at a time
items.say: New version, it swaps them over one at a time.

scenes.text:
Say what should exist.
*It handles the how.*
scenes.say: That's Kubernetes. Say what should exist, and it handles the how.
